_doc: Ground truth for the HARDER corpus (evaluation/fixtures_hard2). This corpus targets the levers DESIGN.md says are untested: cross-file flows whose SINK looks benign in isolation (so per-file analysis should miss them and taint should catch them), one second-order (stored-then-reused) pair, and one check-before-decode ordering pair. Each vulnerable fixture is paired with a structurally look-alike safe twin; [] means any finding is a false positive.

vulnerable/cmdi_benign_helper_crossfile.note: user format -> exec_report -> _run -> os.popen, across app.py/reporting.py; _run looks like generic plumbing in isolation

vulnerable/sqli_second_order.note: nickname stored via a bound param (safe write), later read back and concatenated into SQL in a different handler (second-order)

vulnerable/ssrf_fetch_helper_crossfile.note: user url -> get_json across app.py/httpclient.py; no scheme/host restriction on requests.get

vulnerable/path_traversal_decode_after_c.note: '..' guard runs on the URL-encoded value; unquote() happens after, so %2e%2e%2f bypasses

vulnerable/deser_pickle_crossfile.note: base64 request blob -> load_state across app.py/session.py -> pickle.loads (RCE)

safe/cmdi_listargs_crossfile_safe.note: same cross-file chain shape, but subprocess.run(argv, shell=False) - user value is one literal arg

safe/sqli_second_order_param_safe.note: same store/read-back shape, but the read-back value is bound as a query parameter

safe/ssrf_allowlist_crossfile_safe.note: same cross-file fetch shape, but https + exact host allowlist + redirects disabled

safe/path_traversal_decode_then_check_sa.note: decode first, basename, join under fixed BASE, abspath-prefix confirmed

safe/deser_json_crossfile_safe.note: same decode-then-load_state shape, but json.loads cannot instantiate objects
